Subject: RE: Region pinning & data residency - technical answers (Acme Bank)

Hi Oliver / Marissa / Priya -

Thanks - answering each ask below. Short version up front: tenant-level region pinning is supported for inference and backups on Redwood Dedicated and Private. On Hosted (shared) we can provide region routing for inference but backups and some failover behaviors may be limited; I call that out per item.

1) Tenant-level region pinning (inference + backups)
- Dedicated / Private: yes. We support per-tenant config that restricts inference traffic and snapshot storage to a chosen region (e.g., eu-west-1). Backups remain in the pinned region by default and are not replicated outside the region unless explicitly configured in a Dedicated failover policy.
- Hosted API: we can pin inference routing to a region for requests, but backups (automated snapshots) for shared-hosted customers are stored in our multi-region backup pool and not guaranteed to remain in-region. For strict regulatory requirements, we recommend Dedicated or Private.

2) Cross-region failover behavior
- Dedicated / Private: failover can be configured either automatic or manual. For Acme Bank’s requirement (manual approval before serving from another region), we support a manual failover mode: cluster health triggers an alert; failover requires an operator action via Console or API to enable cross-region routing for the tenant. We can also configure a playbook webhook that notifies your ops team and requires an explicit approve call.
- Hosted: we provide automated regional fallbacks to preserve availability; however, this can expose traffic to other regions and is not suitable where regulatory constraints forbid serving from outside region.

3) Backups & KMS/HSM
- Dedicated / Private: snapshots are encrypted with your customer-managed KMS keys (we support AWS KMS, GCP CMEK patterns, or HSM integrations). By default snapshots are stored in the customer-specified region and we do not replicate them cross-region unless you opt in.
- Hosted: backups are encrypted at rest with provider-managed keys; we can enable envelope encryption for some enterprise customers but CMS keys are only available on Dedicated/Private.

4) Logging & retention
- Audit logs: we produce per-tenant audit events (request metadata, model & route, timestamp, user/actor id if available). Logs can be retained in our platform for configurable windows (30/90/365 days). For Acme’s 1-year retention we can configure 365-day retention on Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Exports: logs can be exported to your SIEM via S3/GCS export or via streaming to a syslog/HTTPS endpoint. We also support periodic snapshots of logs to a customer-controlled bucket for long-term archival.

5) Additional notes on contracts & lead times
- Dedicated: region guarantees + CMK support typically require a Dedicated commitment. Lead time for provisioning dedicated capacity can be 4-8 weeks depending on sizing and region.
- Private (on-prem / VPC): full control over residency and keys; longer onboarding but best for strict regulatory needs.

If helpful I attached the region failover sketch Marissa sent and a short checklist we use for SOC2/regulatory-focused customers. Happy to hop on a short technical walkthrough - I can demo the Console failover toggle and the export flow for logs.
